Revise la creación de procesos y conexiones de red del host en +/- 15 minutos, en especial hijos de user.exe y conexiones salientes nuevas.
Analice los logs de acceso de Tomcat en busca de cargas o solicitudes anómalas previas al evento y sus IP de origen.
Busque alertas anteriores del mismo host y el mismo hash en otros endpoints.

Pruebas de detección o ejercicios de red team que reproduzcan el script en un entorno controlado y autorizado.

en.summary: A PowerShell script block matching the launcher Lace Tempest uses to start its loader after exploiting CVE-2023-47246 in SysAid was logged. Treat the SysAid server as potentially compromised.
en.what_it_detects: Script Block Logging events (4104) whose ScriptBlockText contains all of: \SysAidServer\tomcat\webapps, 'Starting user.exe', \usersfiles\user.exe, 'Remove-Item -Force "$wapps' and '(Sophos).'.
en.why_it_matters: It shows PowerShell execution (ATT&CK T1059.001) on an on-premise SysAid server launching user.exe from the Tomcat webapps folder and then deleting artifacts. This is post-exploitation activity, not scanning.
triage_steps: Read the full ScriptBlockText, including all fragments sharing the same ScriptBlockId, and note referenced paths, commands and files.
Confirm the host runs SysAid Server and check its version against SysAid's CVE-2023-47246 advisory.
Identify the parent of powershell.exe; a java.exe or SysAid Tomcat service parent strengthens the web exploitation hypothesis.
Check for \SysAidServer\tomcat\webapps\usersfiles\user.exe, collect its hash, and review recent WAR or JSP files in webapps.
Review process creation and network connections on the host within +/- 15 minutes, especially user.exe children and new outbound connections.
Search Tomcat access logs for unusual uploads or requests before the event and note source IPs.
Look for earlier alerts on the same host and the same hash on other endpoints.
false_positives: Unlikely per the rule; the string combination is highly specific to the launcher.
Authorized detection tests or red team exercises replaying the script in a controlled environment.
response_steps: Validate the script content and isolate the SysAid server from the network if activity is confirmed.
Preserve evidence: memory, Tomcat logs, 4104 events, and copies of user.exe and webapps files before cleanup.
Remove malicious artifacts only after analysis, apply the SysAid update fixing CVE-2023-47246, and rotate exposed credentials.
Hunt for derived IOCs across the fleet and restore service from a trusted source with heightened monitoring.
en.severity_rationale: High fits because a match requires five specific strings from a known exploitation chain, so false positives are very unlikely.

positive.description: Script block on a SysAid server launching user.exe from webapps and cleaning up, containing all five required strings.

event.ScriptBlockText:
$wapps = "C:\Program Files\SysAidServer\tomcat\webapps"
$av = Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.Name -match "(Sophos)." }
Write-Host "Starting user.exe"
Start-Process "$wapps\usersfiles\user.exe"
Start-Sleep -Seconds 5
Remove-Item -Force "$wapps\usersfiles.war"

negative.description: Legitimate admin maintenance script referencing the SysAid webapps folder but without the launcher strings.
